newsitem.title: USA: New fund first to aim at gay men, women.
newsitem.headline: New fund first to aim at gay men, women.

text.p: In what appears to be the first of its kind, a new mutual fund has been launched that is being marketed directly at homosexual men and women.
The fund buys only securities of companies with policies that it views as "gay friendly."

"We won't invest in companies unless they have a progressive policy towards gays and lesbians," said Shelly Meyers, portfolio manager of the Meyers, Sheppard Pride Fund. She said there was a need in the market for such a fund.

The fund, started in June, looks for companies with personnel policies that explicitly prohibit discrimination based on sexual orientation, and those that offer health benefits to homosexual partners.
Two fund-tracking firms said the fund appears to be the first to have such criteria.

Meyers said the fund has identified about 400 companies that meet its guidelines, including about 200 of those in the Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks. That compares with a total of about 6,000 corporations with publicly traded stock in the United States.

Meyers said she has found that the technology, financial services and consumer services sectors have a higher proportion of companies that are "gay friendly," with utilities and energy among the least friendly.
The fund's investment philosophy is value-oriented, seeking equities that are undervalued, she said.

The Meyers, Sheppard Pride Fund uses so-called momentum investing -- seeking out companies with rising earnings, a change in product mix or a significant management overhaul -- as well as traditional criteria as stock price compared with a company's underlying value.

The fund has about 40 issues in its portfolio, and ranges between 35 and 55 stocks. Meyers estimated that the fund's turnover ratio -- or how often it sells stocks within one year -- will be relatively low, ranging from 30 percent to 75 percent.
Its top five holdings are: Arrow Electronics Inc., McKesson Corp., Time Warner Inc., Glendale Federal Bank and American Express Co.
Meyers said the fund has about $800,000 in total assets. New funds often find it hard to reach $1 million at first, but she said she expected to cross that barrier soon.
She expected assets to grow to about $35 million by next June. The fund is aimed at individual and institutional investors.
Meyers said the firm has made distribution deals with Furman Selz, an investment bank that also markets mutual funds, and Jack White & Co., a discount brokerage.
It also has been negotiating with Charles Schwab, another discount brokerage, about distribution, she said.
